clue.text: No big case for investing funds in underwear

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or enclose, so the underwear wraps round the funds

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underwear
capital is money or funds

explanation.surface: Someone is stuffing their savings into their underwear drawer for safekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No big case' plays on printers' upper case and lower case: small capitals are capital letter shapes, but not big ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Small capitals are a typeface of reduced-height capital letters, neither full upper case nor ordinary lower case.

clue.text: Computer device offering way of working with purpose

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
use means purpose, as in 'what's the use?'

explanation.surface: A gadget is recommended as a purposeful way to get work done.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is the hand-held pointing gadget used with a computer.

clue.text: Permanent party with free food will draw in criminal

indicators.note: to draw in is to pull something inside, so the party takes the criminal within it

parts.note: a lig is a British slang term for a freeloading party with free food and drink
a felon is a criminal

explanation.surface: A lavish free buffet attracts a crook who stays for good.
explanation.walkthrough: LIG is British media slang for a free do laid on by a company, with free food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifelong lasts a whole lifetime, so it is effectively permanent.

clue.text: Copper attending disturbance overlooking last odd item

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: to overlook is to leave out, and 'last' points to the final letter of the disturbance

parts.note: a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: A police officer at a riot ignores the last strange object lying around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal; 'overlooking last' drops the T from RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual object, a curiosity, so an odd item.

clue.text: Wine manuscript is Minister's responsibility

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a folio is a leaf or volume of a manuscript

explanation.surface: A government minister is in charge of a manuscript about wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's portfolio is the department or area of government they are given charge of.

clue.text: Wasted singular legwear

parts.note: wasted and tight are both slang for drunk
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: One odd item of clothing for the legs has been thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting garment covering the legs and hips.

clue.text: Monastery in the morning surrounded by intense light — excellent

indicators.note: something surrounded by another sits inside it, so the morning goes within the light

parts.note: a laser produces an intense beam of light
AM is ante meridiem, in the morning
A1 means excellent, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A monastery is bathed in brilliant light at dawn, and it looks wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamaserai is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery of lamas.

clue.text: Robert and Jack circling area to get tree

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the two names enclose the area

parts.note: Bob is short for Robert
a jack and an AB (able seaman) are both sailors

explanation.surface: Two men walk round a patch of ground to reach a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree with a hugely swollen trunk.

clue.text: Bad reputation Independent assigned to new group of footballers — gosh!

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football
'my!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh!'

explanation.surface: A newspaper is shocked to be linked with a new football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety, being well known for something bad.

clue.text: Water supply American provided in Queens?

indicators.note: the condition word sits in between the two queens

parts.note: two abbreviations for queen, QU and ER (Elizabeth Regina), make the plural
if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: An American supplies water to the New York borough of Queens.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Queens' is not the New York borough but two different queens, QU and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquifer is underground rock holding groundwater that wells can draw on, a natural water source.

clue.text: Pattern of behaviour regarding booze will absorb the writer

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so the drink holds the writer inside it

parts.note: gin is a type of booze
the writer, from the setter's view, is me

explanation.surface: A writer's habits revolve around drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed routine of diet, exercise or conduct, a set way of living.

clue.text: Dice game inappropriate? Scarper!

parts.note: beetle is a party dice game in which players draw a beetle
off means unacceptable or inappropriate, as in 'that was a bit off'

explanation.surface: Someone playing dice in the wrong place is told to run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is a British party game in which dice throws let players draw the parts of a beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle off and to scarper are both informal British ways of saying hurry away.

clue.text: A student group backed scientist

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: L is a learner, from the learner-driver plate
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A group of students supports a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American inventor and physicist behind alternating-current systems.

clue.text: Idea I introduced in local office — crazy, but not initially

indicators.note: something introduced in another is placed inside it, so the letter goes within the office

parts.note: a branch is a local office of a larger firm

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter

parts.note: wild means crazy

explanation.surface: An employee's idea for the local branch sounds mad, but it wasn't at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' strips the W from WILD, leaving ILD.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainchild is an original idea or invention credited to a particular person.

clue.text: Article located in new arrangement following informal comments

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newspaper article has been laid out afresh after some off-the-record remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' shuffles LOCATED into ECDOTAL; 'in' and 'new' look like part of the anagram signal, but 'new' gives its own N.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on personal stories and hearsay rather than systematic study.

clue.text: Distribution of lather is concealing variable result of salon treatment

indicators.note: concealing means hiding within, so the shuffled letters close round the variable
distribution spreads the letters out into a new order

parts.note: Y is a conventional algebraic variable

explanation.surface: How the shampoo foam is spread hides a changeable outcome at the hairdresser's.
explanation.walkthrough: The salon picture makes 'lather' look like part of the definition, but it is anagram fodder: 'Distribution of' shuffles it with 'is', and 'concealing' tucks the Y inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle is the cut and shape a hairdresser gives the hair.

clue.text: Uncertain legal issue for sheltered accommodation?

definitions.meaning: a matter where the rules are unclear
a whimsical reading: a district for ...-haired pensioners, as sheltered housing is for the elderly

explanation.surface: A question about the law concerns a home for older people.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheltered accommodation is British housing for older people with a warden on hand; the question mark marks the joke reading of a place for the grey-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey area is the idiom for a situation that falls between clear rules, neither plainly allowed nor forbidden.

clue.text: My criticism will exclude King and nearly everyone of occult tendencies

indicators.note: to exclude is to leave out, so the king's letter is dropped from the criticism

parts.note: stick means harsh criticism, as in 'taking stick'
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone says their criticism will leave out the King and most other people with occult leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystical describes spiritual or occult matters beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: See 17
Part of quiz: Australian with hesitation about one of her states

indicators.note: the hesitation is placed in relation to the state, here following straight after it

parts.note: NSW is New South Wales, one of Australia's states; 'her' refers back to the Australian
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An Australian contestant hesitates over a quiz question about her home state.
explanation.definitionFit: Every quiz consists of questions and their answers, so an answer is one component of it.

clue.text: I'd be unsettled by toying with miss?

definitions.text: I'd be unsettled by toying with miss?

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed or thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that flirting with a young woman would make them uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: 'unsettled' shuffles TOYING and MISS, and a woman-hater might say exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: A misogynist dislikes women, so dallying with a young woman would discomfort him.

clue.text: Abstract viewpoint those people held about serving men

indicators.note: to be held about is to have something wrapped round it, so the people enclose the soldiers

parts.note: they means those people
OR is other ranks, enlisted soldiers rather than officers

explanation.surface: A group of people holds an abstract opinion about soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a speculative idea or set of principles, as opposed to practice.

clue.text: Currently probing opening not quite resulting in fame

indicators.note: probing means pushing inside, so the word for currently goes into the opening
not quite means falling short by a letter, so the last one is dropped

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
now means currently

explanation.surface: Delving into a near-complete opening brings celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' reads as a time adverb for the whole sentence, but it is a piece; 'not quite' leaves REN, which 'probing' splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is the state of being widely known and celebrated, i.e. fame.

clue.text: League restricted by team in furtive move

indicators.note: being restricted by something is being hemmed in by it, so the league goes inside the team

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A sports team makes a sneaky play within the league's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidle is a sideways, stealthy approach, a move made shyly or furtively.

clue.text: Trivial function to swap leading parts in element of theatre design

indicators.note: the front parts of the two words change places, a Spoonerism

parts.note: light means trivial, as in light entertainment
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A designer jokes that a trivial task means switching the leading roles.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening L and S of LIGHT and SINE gives SIGHT and LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightline is the line of view from a seat to the stage, which theatre architects must plan.

clue.text: Dirty frame amongst frames of gallery?

indicators.note: amongst means in the middle of, so the frame goes between the outer letters
the frames of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: a rim is a frame or border

explanation.surface: A grubby picture frame hangs among the others in an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimy means covered with grime, ingrained dirt.

clue.text: Playwright that is hosting book society (Norway)

indicators.note: hosting means having a guest inside, so the abbreviation for that is holds the book and society

parts.note: ie is id est, that is
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A Norwegian dramatist entertains a literary society.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(Norway)' reads as a nod to the playwright's homeland but also supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Hospital department not looking so good? Measure of disorder here

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
ropy is British slang for poor quality or in poor health

explanation.surface: A hospital ward is looking run-down, a sign of its chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Ropy (or ropey) is everyday British slang for shabby or feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Entropy is the thermodynamic quantity that gauges randomness or chaos in a system.

clue.text: I note canine is gold — and this?

definitions.text: I note canine is gold — and this?

parts.note: C is the dental-chart abbreviation for a canine tooth
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone notices a gold tooth and wonders whether the next one is gold too.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: having noticed a gold canine, the speaker asks about the tooth beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front cutting tooth, next to the canine in the mouth.

clue.text: Swearwords yet to be released when trapped by friendly fire?

indicators.note: being trapped by something means being held inside it, so the shuffled word sits in the middle

parts.note: blanks are harmless cartridges, so a friendly volley is 'blank, blank'

indicators.note: released means freed from its order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Curses not yet aired are caught up in a friendly-fire incident.
explanation.walkthrough: Firing blanks hurts no one, hence 'friendly'; 'to be released' scrambles the word yet into ETY, held by 'when trapped by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blankety-blank is a coy stand-in for omitted swearing, a euphemism for expletives.
